title: Bobby Hackett and the Eddie Condon records
summary: Jones recalls first hearing Bobby Hackett on Jackie Gleason records and Condon albums with Lee Wiley, and Condon's role in the revival.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: You know, now that I was thinking back on it, we were discussing what influence Bobby Hackett was on me. And I can remember now, every night on the radio, maybe 8 o'clock, 9 o'clock at night, I had to be in the late 40s again, 48, 49, or 50. They had an hour of recorded music, sentimental or ballads. And quite often they played the Jackie Gleason records with Bobby Hackett. The original Gleason Hackett things with songs like Alone Together and My Funny Valentine. And that is the first I remember hearing of Bobby Hackett. And I became aware of him as a player. And not too long after that, I got an album of Eddie Condon. And they had different bands on each record. It was the, you know, the 478 albums, the 10-inch records. And they had different players on each record. And on two of the sides were Lee Wiley. And one song she sang was The Man I Love. And I think the other one was Someone To Watch Over Me. And Bobby backed her up on it, as only Bobby could do. And then I believe he was on one, he did one called My One and Only, which was a George Gershman tune.
I don't think I ever owned that album.
I used to buy a lot of Condon records. Of course I used to hear Condon live on the record.
Yeah, see I only heard him once. Live. And that was at his club, the new club downtown. But I listened to his band whenever possible, you know, on records.
Oh yeah. Well, he was a great spokesman during that time.
Oh yes, he did an awful lot for the renaissance of that music. It was going through an upsurge in those days.
